verses.zh: 列国啊，要近前来听！众民哪，要侧耳而听！地和其上所充满的，世界和其中一切所出的都应当听！
verses.en: Come near, you nations, and listen!Pay attention, you people!The earth and everything it contains must listen,the world and everything that lives in it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the world and its offspring”; NASB “the world and all that springs from it.”

verses.zh: 因为耶和华向万国发忿恨，向他们的全军发烈怒，将他们灭尽，交出他们受杀戮。
verses.en: For the Lord is angry at all the nationsand furious with all their armies.He will annihilate them and slaughter them.

verses.zh: 被杀的必然抛弃，尸首臭气上腾；诸山被他们的血融化。
verses.en: Their slain will be left unburied,[NOTE:1] their corpses will stink;[NOTE:2] the hills will soak up their blood.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “will be cast aside”; NASB, NIV “thrown out.”
Heb “[as for] their corpses, their stench will arise.”
Heb “hills will dissolve from their blood.”

verses.zh: 天上的万象都要消没；天被卷起，好像书卷。其上的万象要残败，像葡萄树的叶子残败，又像无花果树的叶子残败一样。
verses.en: All the stars in the sky will fade away,[NOTE:1] the sky will roll up like a scroll;all its stars will wither,like a leaf withers and falls from a vineor a fig withers and falls from a tree.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and all the host of heaven will rot.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa inserts “and the valleys will be split open,” but this reading may be influenced by Mic 1:4. On the other hand, the statement, if original, could have been omitted by homoioarcton, a scribe’s eye jumping from the conjunction prefixed to “the valleys” to the conjunction prefixed to the verb “rot.”
Heb “like the withering of a leaf from a vine, and like the withering from a fig tree.”

verses.zh: 因为我的刀在天上已经喝足；这刀必临到以东和我所咒诅的民，要施行审判。
verses.en: He says,[NOTE:1] “Indeed, my sword has slaughtered heavenly powers.[NOTE:2] Look, it now descends on Edom,[NOTE:3] on the people I will annihilate in judgment.”
notes: The words “he says” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The Lord speaks at this point.

Heb “indeed [or “for”] my sword is drenched in the heavens.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has תראה (“[my sword] appeared [in the heavens]”), but this is apparently an attempt to make sense out of a difficult metaphor. Cf. NIV “My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens.”sn In v. 4 the “host of the heaven” refers to the heavenly luminaries (stars and planets, see, among others, Deut 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kgs 17:16; 21:3, 5; 23:4-5; 2 Chr 33:3, 5) that populate the divine/heavenly assembly in mythological and prescientific Israelite thought (see Job 38:7; Isa 14:13). As in 24:21, they are viewed here as opposing God and being defeated in battle.
Edom is mentioned here as epitomizing the hostile nations that oppose God.

verses.zh: 耶和华的刀满了血，用脂油和羊羔、公山羊的血，并公绵羊腰子的脂油滋润的；因为耶和华在波斯拉有献祭的事，在以东地大行杀戮。
verses.en: The Lord’s sword is dripping with blood,it is covered[NOTE:1] with fat;it drips[NOTE:2] with the blood of young rams and goatsand is covered[NOTE:3] with the fat of rams’ kidneys.For the Lord is holding a sacrifice[NOTE:4] in Bozrah,[NOTE:5] a bloody[NOTE:6] slaughter in the land of Edom.
notes: The verb is a rare Hotpaal passive form. See GKC 150 §54.h.
The words “it drips” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
The words “and is covered” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “for there is a sacrifice to the Lord.”
The Lord’s judgment of Edom is compared to a bloody sacrificial scene.
Heb “great” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 野牛、牛犊，和公牛要一同下来。他们的地喝醉了血；他们的尘土因脂油肥润。
verses.en: Wild oxen will be slaughtered[NOTE:1] along with them,as well as strong bulls.[NOTE:2] Their land is drenched with blood,their soil is covered with fat.
notes: Heb “will go down”; NAB “shall be struck down.”
Heb “and bulls along with strong ones.” Perhaps this refers to the leaders.

verses.zh: 因耶和华有报仇之日，为锡安的争辩有报应之年。
verses.en: For the Lord has planned a day of revenge,[NOTE:1] a time when he will repay Edom for her hostility toward Zion.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for a day of vengeance [is] for the Lord.”

Heb “a year of repayment for the strife of Zion.” The translation assumes that רִיב (riv) refers to Edom’s hostility toward Zion. Another option is to understand רִיב (riv) as referring to the Lord’s taking up Zion’s cause. In this case one might translate, “a time when he will repay Edom and vindicate Zion.”

verses.zh: 以东的河水要变为石油，尘埃要变为硫磺；地土成为烧着的石油，
verses.en: Edom’s[NOTE:1] streams will be turned into pitchand her soil into brimstone;her land will become burning pitch.
notes: Heb “her”; the referent (Edom) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 昼夜总不熄灭，烟气永远上腾，必世世代代成为荒废，永永远远无人经过。
verses.en: Night and day it will burn;[NOTE:1] its smoke will ascend continually.Generation after generation it will be a wasteland,and no one will ever pass through it again.
notes: Heb “it will not be extinguished.”

verses.zh: 鹈鹕、箭猪却要得为业；猫头鹰、乌鸦要住在其间。耶和华必将空虚的准绳，混沌的线铊，拉在其上。
verses.en: Owls and wild animals[NOTE:1] will live there,[NOTE:2] all kinds of wild birds[NOTE:3] will settle in it.The Lord[NOTE:4] will stretch out over herthe measuring line of ruinand the plumb line[NOTE:5] of destruction.[NOTE:6]
notes: קָאַת (qaʾat) refers to some type of bird (cf. Lev 11:18; Deut 14:17) that was typically found near ruins (see Zeph 2:14). קִפּוֹד (qippod) may also refer to a type of bird (NAB “hoot owl”; NIV “screech owl”; TEV “ravens”), but some have suggested a rodent may be in view (cf. NCV “small animals”; ASV “porcupine”; NASB, NRSV “hedgehog”).
Heb “will possess it” (so NIV).
The Hebrew text has יַנְשׁוֹף וְעֹרֵב (yanshof veʿorev). Both the יַנְשׁוֹף (“owl”; see Lev 11:17; Deut 14:16) and עֹרֵב (“raven”; Lev 11:15; Deut 14:14) were types of wild birds.
Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “stones,” i.e., the stones used in a plumb bob.
The metaphor in v. 11b emphasizes that God has carefully planned Edom’s demise.

verses.zh: 以东人要召贵胄来治国；那里却无一个，首领也都归于无有。
verses.en: Her nobles will have nothing left to call a kingdom,and all her officials will disappear.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “will be nothing”; NCV, TEV, NLT “will all be gone.”

verses.zh: 以东的宫殿要长荆棘；保障要长蒺藜和刺草；要作野狗的住处，鸵鸟的居所。
verses.en: Her fortresses will be overgrown with thorns;thickets and weeds will grow[NOTE:1] in her fortified cities.Jackals will settle there;ostriches will live there.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “will grow” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

Heb “and she will be a settlement for wild dogs, a dwelling place for ostriches.” The translation assumes an emendation of חָצִיר (khatsir, “grass”) to חָצֵר (khatser, “settlement”). One of the Qumran scrolls of Isaiah (1QIsaa) supports this emendation (cf. HALOT 344 s.v. II חָצִיר)

verses.zh: 旷野的走兽要和豺狼相遇；野山羊要与伴偶对叫。夜间的怪物必在那里栖身，自找安歇之处。
verses.en: Wild animals and wild dogs will congregate there;[NOTE:1] wild goats will bleat to one another.[NOTE:2] Yes, nocturnal animals[NOTE:3] will rest thereand make for themselves a nest.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “will meet” (so NIV); NLT “will mingle there.”
Heb “and a goat will call to its neighbor.”

The precise meaning of לִילִית (lilit) is unclear, though in this context the word certainly refers to some type of wild animal or bird. The word appears to be related to לַיְלָה (laylah, “night”). Some interpret it as the name of a female night demon, on the basis of an apparent Akkadian cognate used as the name of a demon. Later Jewish legends also identified Lilith as a demon. Cf. NRSV “Lilith.”
Heb “and will find for themselves a resting place.”

verses.zh: 箭蛇要在那里做窝，下蛋，菢蛋，生子，聚子在其影下；鹞鹰各与伴偶聚集在那里。
verses.en: Owls[NOTE:1] will make nests and lay eggs[NOTE:2] there;they will hatch them and protect them.[NOTE:3] Yes, hawks[NOTE:4] will gather there,each with its mate.
notes: Hebrew קִפּוֹז (qippoz) occurs only here; the precise meaning of the word is uncertain.
For this proposed meaning for Hebrew מָלַט (malat), see HALOT 589 s.v. I מלט.
Heb “and brood [over them] in her shadow.”
The precise meaning of דַּיָּה (dayyah) is uncertain, though the term appears to refer to some type of bird of prey, perhaps a vulture.

verses.zh: 你们要查考宣读耶和华的书。这都无一缺少，无一没有伴偶；因为我的口已经吩咐，他的灵将他们聚集。
verses.en: Carefully read the scroll of the Lord![NOTE:1] Not one of these creatures will be missing,[NOTE:2] none will lack a mate.[NOTE:3] For the Lord has issued the decree,[NOTE:4] and his own Spirit gathers them.[NOTE:5]
notes: It is uncertain what particular scroll is referred to here. Perhaps the phrase simply refers to this prophecy and is an admonition to pay close attention to the details of the message. tn Heb “Seek from upon the scroll of the Lord and read.”

Heb “one from these will not be missing.” הֵנָּה (hennah, “these”) is feminine plural in the Hebrew text. It may refer only to the birds mentioned in v. 15b or may include all of the creatures listed in vv. 14b-15 (all of which are identified with feminine nouns).
Heb “each its mate they will not lack.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “for a mouth, it has commanded.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa and a few medieval mss have פִּיהוּ (pihu, “his mouth [has commanded]”), while a few other medieval mss read פִּי יְהוָה (pi yehvah, “the mouth of the Lord [has commanded]”).

Heb “and his spirit, he gathers them.” The pronominal suffix (“them”) is feminine plural, referring to the birds mentioned in v. 15b or to all of the creatures listed in vv. 14b-15 (all of which are identified with feminine nouns).

verses.zh: 他也为他们拈阄，又亲手用准绳给他们分地；他们必永得为业，世世代代住在其间。
verses.en: He assigns them their allotment;[NOTE:1] he measures out their assigned place.[NOTE:2] They will live there[NOTE:3] permanently;they will settle in it through successive generations.
notes: Heb “and he causes the lot to fall for them.” Once again the pronominal suffix (“them”) is feminine plural, referring to the birds mentioned in v. 15b or to all of the creatures listed in vv. 14b-15 (all of which are identified with feminine nouns).

Heb “and his hand divides for them with a measuring line.” The pronominal suffix (“them”) now switches to masculine plural, referring to all the animals and birds mentioned in vv. 11-15, some of which were identified with masculine nouns. This signals closure for this portion of the speech, which began in v. 11. The following couplet (v. 17b) forms an inclusio with v. 11a through verbal repetition.
Heb “will possess it” (so NIV); NCV “they will own that land forever.”
